title: Four-board full-conversion teacher control
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The old four-board positive mirror signal either reflects useful concentrated high-resolution targets or a truncation artifact. Repeating the exact board split with all sharded rows will distinguish these explanations while holding solver checkpoints and distillation fixed.
material_change: Use only boards 0-3 from the corrected full eight-board compact directories; train H64/source-KL1/residual-L2=.01 dual-mask adapters for three epochs with boards 2/3 as validation/test, then evaluate epoch2/3 on the fixed mirror seed.
baseline: Old truncated four-board dual-mask epoch3 mirror10k +2.005 +/-0.631 but fresh5k -41.98; corrected full eight-board epoch2 mirror4096 -0.623 +/-0.810.

result.summary: The corrected full-sharded four-board epoch2 adapter passed the 10k paired internal gate at +1.4486 bb/100 CI95 +/-0.5574, but the same frozen SHA scored -9.4359 bb/100 over 4,999 fresh independent Slumbot hands, CI95 [-51.3721,+32.5003].
result.conclusion: Restoring all converter rows did not reproduce the prior catastrophic external loss and improved substantially over the earlier dual-mask candidate, but the frozen policy remains negative and statistically unresolved externally. Session independence passed; one requested hand was skipped after a documented socket-exhaustion API failure. The checkpoint does not qualify for scaling or a strength claim.
result.next_step: Stop at this safe point. Before any new experiment, repair baseline/report defaults and experiment provenance/accounting; then explicitly choose between one deeper CFR convergence control and a mainline shift to genuine self-play/opponent-league learned-weight training.
